findings.description: Override behavior is not pinned per refusal class. F001 clearly fail-closes corrupt registry loads, but also says an explicit override proceeds after evidence, leaving ambiguity over whether wrong path, unhealthy binding, swapped repo, indeterminate git state, and corrupt registry are all overrideable or whether some are absolute stops.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit overrideability matrix: wrong-worktree may override with durable evidence; evidence-write failure and corrupt registry should likely remain non-overrideable; swapped or unhealthy binding should be explicitly allowed or denied.

findings.description: F002 does not specify or test what happens if registry binding deletion fails after the audit entry is flushed and after git worktree removal starts or succeeds. That leaves a cleanup path where the worktree can be gone but the registry still records a binding, which undermines the clean_removed_audited outcome.
findings.recommendation: Pin the registry mutation ordering and failure behavior, with a fixture for registry-delete/write failure that proves no destructive filesystem removal happens unless the implementation can complete the registry update safely.

findings.description: The journey state names divergent_refused, but F003 says default create only detects and reports divergent allowlisted files, reserving refusal for copy-time overwrite attempts. The intended user-facing result for no-flag divergence is therefore ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether default create with a divergent allowlisted file should succeed with an explicit notice or refuse; then rename the journey state or add the missing refusal acceptance test accordingly.
